changes.current_line: Built for developers: launch payments fast with our APIs, docs and sandbox.
changes.change: For engineering-led marketplace deals: 'Have one of your engineers build your sitter pay flow in our sandbox this weekend, and bring it to Monday standup.' Make the hands-on sandbox build an explicit early step in the evaluation instead of a passing claim.
changes.why: The deal went from bake-off to 'when' only after a customer engineer built a working sitter payment flow in the sandbox over a weekend, and the rep didn't know it had happened, so the proof should be offered on purpose rather than left to chance.

changes.current_line: Onboard, verify and pay out to sellers worldwide, in their local currency.
changes.change: For gig and service apps: 'Keep your paid-by-Friday promise in every country, without a payments team.' Use their words: 'sitter pay' (or their name for their workers) instead of 'payouts', and 'the app' instead of 'marketplace'. Keep onboarding, identity checks and local-currency pay as the supporting detail.
changes.why: The marketplace capability landed on substance, but the customer describes it as 'sitter pay' and 'paid by Friday' and frames the pain as 'payments shouldn't be a team'; sitter pay timing was also the CFO's only question, so this is the phrase both buyers share.

changes.change: Add a 'What you keep when you switch' line for buyers moving off Braintree, covering PayPal and Venmo buttons and saved-card migration. Get the confirmed answer from product/solutions engineering first, and pair it with a named customer of comparable size who migrated saved cards without losing them. Do not publish the line until both exist.
changes.why: After the incumbent's call, the questions shifted to 'what do we lose', and we had no answer on Venmo and no same-size saved-card migration reference, so the risk carried into implementation.

changes.current_line: Customers see an average uplift in authorization rates with Authorization Boost and Adaptive Acceptance.
changes.change: For low-ticket marketplaces, stop leading with authorization-rate uplift. Move it to the appendix and use the sandbox build and sitter pay in its place.
changes.why: The buyer dismissed it outright ('our average booking is 38 dollars, I'm not losing sleep over auth rates') because their pain was paying sitters, not authorizing owners.
